title: Essential Verb - {venir} (to come)
description: Master arrival through active recall and composition practice!
can_do: Express coming and arriving (I come, you come, they come)
Say 'I come from Paris' or 'Who is coming?'
Use venir with vouloir and pouvoir

vocabulary.gloss: I come back / I'm coming back
are you coming to see me?

concepts.definition: Essential irregular verb for coming or arriving! One of the most common verbs in French. Used constantly in conversation.
concepts.example: 'I am coming' ({Je viens}), 'Who is coming?' ({Qui vient?}), 'I come from Paris' ({Je viens de Paris})

concepts.definition: Notice the pattern: je/tu both use '{viens}', then il/elle use '{vient}', nous uses '{venons}', and ils/elles use '{viennent}' with double 'n'!
concepts.example: {je viens}, {tu viens}, {il vient}, {nous venons}, {vous venez}, {ils viennent}

concepts.definition: Combine venir with previous modules for infinite expressions. For example, to say 'I want to come' you can say '{je veux venir}'.
concepts.example: {je viens + de ça, nous venons + avec vous, ils viennent + voir}

concepts.definition: Adding 're-' to a verb means 'again' or 'back'. So '{revenir}' means 'to come back' or 'to return'. It follows the same conjugation pattern as '{venir}' - just add 're-' before each form!
concepts.example: {venir} → {revenir} (to come → to come back), {je viens} → {je reviens}, {il vient} → {il revient}

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{je}'.

mistakes.feedback: Je takes '{viens}', not 'vient'. Remember: je viens, il vient
That's 'you come', not 'I come'. Focus on the pronoun!

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{tu}'.

mistakes.feedback: Tu takes '{viens}', not 'vient'. Pattern: je viens, tu viens

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{il}'.

mistakes.feedback: Il takes '{vient}', not 'viens'. Remember: il vient, elle vient

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{elle}'.

mistakes.feedback: Elle takes '{vient}', not 'viens'. Same as il vient

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{nous}' (regular -ons ending).

mistakes.feedback: Nous takes '{venons}', not 'viens'. Completely different!
Nous takes '{venons}', not 'vient'. Regular -ons pattern!

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{vous}' (regular -ez ending).

mistakes.feedback: Vous takes '{venez}', not 'viens'. Regular -ez pattern!
Vous takes '{venez}', not 'vient'. Remember: vous venez

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{ils}' with double 'n'.

mistakes.feedback: Ils takes '{viennent}', not 'viens'. Double 'n'!
Ils takes '{viennent}', not 'vient'. Double 'n'!

items.hint: Conjugate '{venir}' in the present for '{elles}' with double 'n'.

mistakes.feedback: Elles takes '{viennent}', not 'viens'. Double 'n'!
Elles takes '{viennent}', not 'vient'. Double 'n'!

items.situation: Say that you are coming with that
items.hint: Start with 'I come' in French, then add 'with that'.

mistakes.feedback: Je takes '{viens}', not 'vient'. Remember: je viens, il vient

items.situation: Say where you are coming from
items.cue: I am coming from my house
items.hint: Start with 'I come from' in French, then add 'my house'.

mistakes.feedback: Je takes '{viens}', not 'vient'. Remember: je viens, il vient.

items.situation: Say what he does with her cat
items.cue: He is coming with her cat
items.hint: Start with 'he comes' in French, then add 'with her cat'.

mistakes.feedback: Il takes '{vient}', not 'viens'. Remember: il vient, elle vient

items.hint: Start with 'we come' in French, then add 'with you'.

mistakes.feedback: Nous takes '{venons}', not 'viens'. Completely different!

items.hint: Use '{qui}' as the subject and conjugate '{venir}' like '{il/elle}'.

mistakes.feedback: Use '{qui}' for 'who', not 'quoi'. Try: qui vient?

items.situation: Ask where someone is coming from
items.hint: Use '{d'où}' (from where) and conjugate '{venir}' for '{tu}'.

mistakes.feedback: Need '{de}' with 'où'! Try: d'où viens-tu?
In questions with inversion, you must use a hyphen: d'où viens-tu?

accept: avec quoi est-ce que tu viens?
items.hint: Use '{avec quoi}' (with what) and conjugate '{venir}' for '{tu}'.

mistakes.feedback: Need '{avec}'! Try: avec quoi viens-tu?
In questions with inversion, you must use a hyphen: avec quoi viens-tu?

items.situation: Say what you want to come
items.hint: Use '{vouloir}' in the present for '{je}' + infinitive '{venir}'.

mistakes.feedback: This needs vouloir! Try: je veux venir
When you use two verbs together in French, the second one usually stays in the infinitive. Here: je veux venir.

items.situation: Ask if someone wants to come
items.hint: Turn 'you want to come' into a yes/no question with '{tu}' and '{venir}'.

mistakes.feedback: This needs vouloir! Try: veux-tu venir?
In questions with inversion, you must use a hyphen: veux-tu venir?
When two verbs go together, the second one stays in the infinitive. Here: veux-tu venir?

items.situation: Say what you want to come with
items.cue: I want to come with that
items.hint: Use '{vouloir}' in the present for '{je}' + infinitive '{venir}' + 'with that'.

mistakes.feedback: This needs vouloir! Try: je veux venir avec ça
When you chain two verbs, the second verb should be in the infinitive. Here: je veux venir avec ça.

items.hint: Use '{pouvoir}' in the present for '{tu}' + infinitive '{venir}' and make it a question.

mistakes.feedback: This needs pouvoir! Try: peux-tu venir?
In questions with inversion, you must use a hyphen: peux-tu venir?
In verb + verb combinations, the second verb stays in the infinitive. Here: peux-tu venir?

items.cue: I can come to the hotel
items.hint: Use '{pouvoir}' in the present for '{je}' + infinitive '{venir}' + 'to the hotel'.

mistakes.feedback: This needs pouvoir! Try: je peux venir à l'hôtel
With two verbs together, keep the second one in the infinitive. Here: je peux venir à l'hôtel.

items.situation: Say what you come to see
items.cue: I am coming to see you
items.hint: Use '{venir}' in the present for '{je}' + infinitive '{voir}' + 'you'.

mistakes.feedback: Use the pronoun before the verb: je viens te voir.
In verb + verb structures, the second verb is infinitive. Here: je viens te voir.

items.situation: Ask why someone is coming to see you
items.cue: Why are you coming to see me?
items.hint: Use '{pourquoi}' to ask 'why' and '{venir}' in the present for '{tu}' plus 'to see me' (me voir).

mistakes.feedback: Use the present for 'are coming': pourquoi viens-tu me voir?
In questions with inversion, you must use a hyphen: pourquoi viens-tu me voir?
